title.rendered: A Rest Still Remaining for the People of God | Living from Rest, Day 2

excerpt.rendered: Hebrews 4:9 says a Sabbath rest still remains for the people of God. Day 2 of Living from Rest asks why that promise has not expired, and what it is for.

content.rendered:
God is not out of promises. The rest He prepared is still open, still waiting, still available this morning. The question is only whether we will enter it.

The Gospel For Today | Monday, November 2, 2026 | Living from Rest, Day 2

Today’s Scripture

“There remains therefore a rest for the people of God. For he who has entered His rest has himself also ceased from his works as God did from His. Let us therefore be diligent to enter that rest, lest anyone fall according to the same example of disobedience.”
Hebrews 4:9-11 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Hebrews chapter four is the chapter in the New Testament that makes rest a doctrine, not just a mood. The writer of Hebrews is talking to believers, people already in Christ, and he tells them something astonishing: there is a rest that still remains. Not just the Sabbath of creation. Not just the Promised Land Joshua led Israel into. Something more. A rest the people of God are invited into, right now, on this side of the cross.

Hebrews 4:9, in the NKJV, puts it in one short line: “There remains therefore a rest for the people of God.” The AMPC expands it: “So then, there is still awaiting a full and complete Sabbath-rest reserved for the [true] people of God.” The TPT says, “So there must be a true rest still waiting for believers to experience.”

Three things stand out. First, this rest is reserved. It did not run out when the first generation missed it. Hebrews 3 and 4 tell the story of Israel in the wilderness, how a whole generation refused to believe God and so did not enter the Promised Land. But Hebrews says: do not conclude from that story that the door is closed. The door is still open. The invitation is still live. “There remains” is a strong, present-tense word.

Second, this rest is for the people of God. If you are in Christ, this is for you. It is not for the super-mature. It is not for the ones who have earned it. It is for anyone who has come to Jesus by faith. Day 1 was the invitation. Day 2 is the confirmation that the invitation still works.

Third, this rest is Sabbath-shaped. God rested on the seventh day of creation, not because He was tired, but because the work was finished. The believer’s rest is shaped the same way. We rest, not because our work is done, but because Christ’s work is done. Our rest is a response to a finished cross. “It is finished,” Jesus said, and the invitation to rest flows out from that.

Verse 10 says the one who has entered His rest has himself ceased from his works. That is the clue to what tomorrow’s devotional will unpack: there is a kind of striving we are called to lay down. If you have been performing for God, trying to prove your value by output, trying to secure His favour by your labour, Hebrews 4 is for you. The rest is still remaining. Enter it.

Why This Rest Is Different

It is already prepared. You are not building the room. God has furnished it.

It is based on what Jesus finished. Your rest rides on His cross, not your effort.

It is still open. No matter how long you have run, the door has not closed.

Declaration

I thank God this morning that there remains a rest for me as a child of God. The rest has not expired. The door has not closed. The invitation is live. By faith, I step into the rest Jesus bought with His blood. I cease from striving to earn what He has already given me. I rest in His finished work, and from that rest I will live this day. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
